items.claim: Explicit 'think step by step' is not a universal improvement
items.evidence: Current reasoning-model guidance says simple/direct prompting often works better and explicit CoT can hinder some reasoning models.
items.implication: Treat CoT as model/task-specific historical technique; A/B instead of global prompt rule.

items.claim: Intrinsic self-correction can worsen answers
items.evidence: Critical self-correction literature finds same-model correction without reliable external feedback can degrade reasoning, though other papers find prompt-conditional gains.
items.implication: Store the disagreement; reflection proposes revisions but independent evidence decides replacement.

items.claim: More context is not automatically better
items.evidence: Long-context models can underuse information depending on position and distractors; irrelevant context consumes attention/tokens.
items.implication: Optimize context utility and position; use retrieval/progressive disclosure.

items.claim: Nominal context length is not usable-context quality
items.evidence: Context-extension methods increase addressable tokens but do not prove reliable reasoning/retrieval throughout the window.
items.implication: Benchmark passkey, multi-hop, position sensitivity, and real Agent OS tasks before relying on long window.

items.claim: More retrieval can reduce answer quality
items.evidence: Low-relevance or contradictory chunks can distract generation and increase hallucination surface.
items.implication: Tune top-k/reranking and support abstention; do not optimize recall alone.

items.claim: GraphRAG/knowledge graphs are not automatically superior to hybrid search
items.evidence: Graph indexing is expensive and most local lookup tasks do not need global community synthesis.
items.implication: Benchmark graph-specific query classes before adding graph infrastructure.

items.claim: More memory can create memory pollution
items.evidence: Long-term memory requires update, abstention, temporal reasoning, and relevance—not maximum retention.
items.implication: Measure retrieval quality and forgotten-needed rate; stage promotion and archive stale derived state.

items.claim: Generated summaries can fossilize interpretation errors
items.evidence: Hierarchical memory/context compression may amplify an early wrong summary across later retrieval.
items.implication: Keep canonical source/evidence addressable; summaries are derived and re-buildable.

items.claim: Synthetic training data is not free improvement
items.evidence: Recursive reliance on generated data can lose distribution tails/model quality.
items.implication: Maintain real/reference anchors, provenance, dedupe, filtering and protected holdout.

items.claim: More training data can be worse than better-selected data
items.evidence: LIMA, AlpaGasus, LESS and dedup studies show noisy/redundant volume can underperform smaller targeted/high-quality data.
items.implication: Optimize information quality/coverage before corpus size.

items.claim: A larger model is not always better value
items.evidence: Task difficulty, validator strength, latency and price determine cost per successful task.
items.implication: Route by task-specific measured threshold, not model prestige.

items.claim: Higher reasoning effort is not always better
items.evidence: Reasoning effort trades tokens/latency for quality and should be task-dependent.
items.implication: Benchmark effort sweep by task family and escalate on evidence.

items.claim: More agents are not automatically better
items.evidence: Multi-agent architectures introduce coordination/token overhead and are poor fits for tightly coupled tasks.
items.implication: Fan out only separable work; compare against strong single-agent baseline.

items.claim: Multi-agent debate does not automatically cancel evaluator bias
items.evidence: Research finds some debate/judge setups amplify biases.
items.implication: Preserve disagreement and calibrate against human/deterministic evidence.

items.claim: Majority vote can confidently preserve correlated errors
items.evidence: Self-consistency only helps if samples have useful diversity and aggregation correlates with truth.
items.implication: Measure marginal accuracy vs N and error correlation; use verifier when possible.

items.claim: LLM-as-judge is not an objective oracle
items.evidence: Judges show position and other biases and can share the generator's blind spots.
items.implication: Randomize order, calibrate with humans, add deterministic anchors, allow abstention.

items.claim: A single composite benchmark score invites Goodhart effects
items.evidence: Aggregate score can hide critical safety, reliability or cost regressions.
items.implication: Maintain primary user outcomes plus explicit guardrail metrics and failure breakdown.

items.claim: Public benchmark leadership may not predict Agent OS workload quality
items.evidence: Benchmark distributions differ from real tasks and contamination can invalidate comparisons.
items.implication: Use private/dynamic workload suites and champion/challenger shadow tests.

items.claim: Prompt optimization can overfit the evaluator
items.evidence: Automated search methods optimize whichever metric/judge they see, including its biases.
items.implication: Separate train/dev/holdout and security gates; never optimize on protected holdout.

items.claim: Emotional/stakes prompting is not a production reliability mechanism
items.evidence: EmotionPrompt reported gains in a historical model set, but mechanism/generalization are unclear.
items.implication: Preserve as prompt-sensitivity evidence; do not use manipulative stakes language as a quality guarantee.

items.claim: Re-reading the question is not a universal free win
items.evidence: Re2 duplicates input and likely depends strongly on model architecture/version.
items.implication: Cheap A/B only; remove if no measured gain.

items.claim: Generated-knowledge/recitation can turn hallucination into pseudo-evidence
items.evidence: Closed-book knowledge elicitation may improve benchmark recall but has no authoritative grounding.
items.implication: Use retrieval for current/high-stakes facts; tag generated knowledge as synthetic.

items.claim: Chain-of-Verification is not equivalent to external fact checking
items.evidence: Same-model verification can share the original model's factual blind spots.
items.implication: Answer verification questions through independent sources/tools where possible.

items.claim: Tool availability can reduce performance if schemas overload context
items.evidence: Large tool catalogs consume context and create tool-selection confusion.
items.implication: Eager-load common tools, defer/search rare ones, evaluate tool catalog size.

items.claim: Deferred tool discovery has overhead and failure modes
items.evidence: Tool search saves schema context but adds a discovery step and relies on namespace descriptions.
items.implication: Use only when catalog size/usage distribution justify it.

items.claim: Caching without complete dependency keys is a correctness bug
items.evidence: A high cache hit rate is harmful if stale outputs are reused after semantic changes.
items.implication: Version processors/dependencies and test invalidation before optimizing hit rate.

items.claim: Retries can amplify failures and side effects
items.evidence: Nested/unbounded retries multiply cost and can repeat writes.
items.implication: Bound retries, classify transient errors, use idempotency and operation identity.

items.claim: Streaming/background execution can make partial/provisional state look final
items.evidence: Long-running UX can expose incomplete output before validation.
items.implication: Label provisional vs validated and gate actions on final state.

items.claim: Compaction is lossy state transformation unless proven otherwise
items.evidence: Provider or model summaries can omit constraints or decisions.
items.implication: Preserve objective, decisions, IDs and canonical external state independently; regression-test compaction.

items.claim: Model editing scales poorly without strong safeguards
items.evidence: ROME/MEMIT-style repeated edits can cause forgetting and downstream degradation.
items.implication: Prefer external Agent OS memory for mutable facts; require reversibility/holdouts for any weight edits.

items.claim: Activation steering is behavior manipulation, not a deterministic policy boundary
items.evidence: CAA/RepE can shift behavior but does not guarantee every output/action complies.
items.implication: Use only as research/defense-in-depth; authorization remains deterministic.

items.claim: Quantization speed/quality claims are deployment-specific
items.evidence: AWQ/GPTQ/SmoothQuant gains depend on model, kernel, hardware and workload.
items.implication: Benchmark exact device/model/task; register quantized deployment separately.

items.claim: Speculative decoding is not universally faster
items.evidence: Speedup depends on draft acceptance, batch size, memory and hardware; complexity may outweigh benefit.
items.implication: Profile real serving regime before adoption.

items.claim: Fine-tuning can be inferior to retrieval, tools or prompt changes for changing requirements
items.evidence: Training adds data governance, regression and migration costs.
items.implication: Escalate to training only after cheaper application-layer mechanisms plateau.

items.claim: Preference optimization has no universal best loss
items.evidence: DPO, KTO, SimPO, ORPO, SLiC-HF, RRHF and newer RL methods make different assumptions/tradeoffs.
items.implication: Benchmark on target behavior and retain base-capability/safety guardrails.

items.claim: Process supervision success on math does not prove general process transparency
items.evidence: Step labels can improve reasoning performance without proving model explanations are faithful internal reasoning.
items.implication: Treat process supervision as task optimization/evaluation evidence, not interpretability proof.

items.claim: Weak-to-strong supervision only partially recovers stronger capability
items.evidence: Naive weak labels can improve strong models but do not recover full latent capability.
items.implication: Do not trust weak automated graders alone for tasks beyond their competence.

items.claim: More explanations can increase over-reliance
items.evidence: Human-facing explanations/confidence can make users trust automation even when it is wrong.
items.implication: Show evidence, verification status and failure modes; evaluate appropriate reliance, not perceived confidence.

items.claim: Proactivity can become negative value through interruption
items.evidence: Useful content delivered at the wrong time/channel creates cognitive cost and alert fatigue.
items.implication: Optimize intervention utility net of interruption; candidate/digest/do-nothing are valid outcomes.

items.claim: The improvement engine can itself become toil
items.evidence: Repeated audits/research/backlog generation without measured accepted changes consumes tokens and attention.
items.implication: Track meta-overhead and research-to-verified-value conversion; simplify or pause when ROI falls.
